1	---
2	name: decode-at-depth-after-p15
3	description: "Decode rates against context depth after P16 (2026-09-22): 34.4 tok/s at depth zero, 31.5 at 128k, the wide-batch cost that was a padding bug, the four depth terms and the control knobs."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: dedbcc64-a855-44f2-a0fa-3d37d0946061
8	  modified: 2026-09-22T15:25:15.756Z
9	---
10	
11	**P17 (2026-09-22) adds ~2% at depth** (128k 31.62 → 32.21, 64k 32.17 →
12	32.97, bit-identical: heads-on-rows at one row folds the same cells in the same
13	order, and the mask dispatch is deleted). **P17-3** takes decode's `attn.select` at
14	128k from 54.0 to 43.8 µs a layer: keys held in registers (`KREG`) plus a 10-bit
15	digit, exact, decode 32.93 → 33.16. Control `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=base`. What
16	is left of the select is ~13 µs of emit/setup. **The host n-gram gather at
17	decode is a tail**: median 236 µs, but 2 of 32 steps take ~8.7 ms at fixed token
18	positions, with ordinary fault counts and no GC, and those are 75% of the line. It
19	did not reproduce in isolation, and explaining it needs a kernel trace this
20	account can't take. `MADV_WILLNEED` is inert, and a pre-read table does not survive
21	staging, so the practical fix is residency, a deployment decision.
22	
23	**Quote this table for decode — P16's (2026-09-22), not P15's.** 48 layers,
24	shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, two passes to
25	0.3%, write-up `research/p16-decode-arena-width.md`.
26	
27	| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | P15 tg |
28	|------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|
29	| 0 | 1155.8 | **34.39** | 29.73 |
30	| 8 000 | 973.9 | 33.54 | 28.78 |
31	| 32 000 | 919.7 | 33.20 | 28.72 |
32	| 64 000 | 896.3 | 32.41 | 28.14 |
33	| 128 000 | 834.4 | **31.53** | 27.20 |
34	
35	At ubatch 4096 (`-ctx 141000`, three depths — five overflow the descriptor):
36	0 → 1292.5 / 33.01, 64k → 979.4 / 33.00, **128k → 904.6 / 31.63**.
37	
38	**P16's lesson, which generalises: a knob that costs decode is found by a
39	per-label diff between the two arms, not by theorising.** The wide-arena cost
40	was blamed on memory residency for two passes (P12-7, P15); `-depth -ubatch`
41	(arena rows separate from `-pp`) showed it followed the arena, and the label
42	diff put all of it on `move`, `dn.qkv`, `attn.qkv` in one look — the input
43	ports padded a one-row decode step with zeros to the whole arena. A padding
44	that is *correct* and slow is invisible to every tolerance test; it is gated
45	now by `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena`. Also P16: `hc.cn` runs a workgroup a
46	(token, stream) at ≤ 64 rows (`LLM_HC_CN_SPLIT_ROWS`, 0 = P11's grid), and
47	`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks (68 → 55 µs at 128k); its passes are neither
48	load-latency- nor atomic-contention-bound (both measured, 0.96x and 0.69x).
49	
50	**The P15 section below still stands for what it explains** (the four depth
51	terms), with P16's rates on top.
52	
53	**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
54	the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
55	4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:
56	
57	- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
58	- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
59	- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
60	- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
61	  depth-scaling term left on the device
62	
63	**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
64	sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
65	per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
66	exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
67	line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
68	host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**
69	
70	**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:
71	
72	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
73	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
74	    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
75	    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
76	    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step
77	
78	**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
79	[[context-depth-rates]]):
80	
81	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
82	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
83	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch
84	
85	**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
86	test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
87	because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
88	that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
89	the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
90	with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
91	2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
92	mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.
93	
94	**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
95	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
96	[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
97	~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.
98	---
99	name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
100	description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
101	metadata:
102	  type: project
103	---
104	
105	**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
106	24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
107	measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
108	places).
109	
110	The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
111	**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
112	…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
113	single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
114	once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
115	wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
116	`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
117	where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.
118	
119	So at decode:
120	
121	- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
122	  concurrently.
123	- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
124	  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
125	  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
126	  nothing.)
127	- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
128	  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.
129	
130	Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
131	[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
132	`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.
133	
134	**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
135	grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
136	length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
137	is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
138	bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.
139	
140	**A prefill-shaped grid breaks this rule silently** (P16, 2026-09-22): P11
141	merged `hc.cn` to one workgroup a token for prefill bandwidth, which at decode
142	made it one workgroup walking four streams — 25 µs where a stream a workgroup
143	is 7. When a kernel is re-gridded for prefill, re-time it at `rows == 1`.
144

146	name: kernels-vertical-reopened
147	description: "The kernel-optimisation vertical was reopened 2026-09-29 as root KERNELS.md (G-stages); the ceiling is per clock, and cmd/probe is the ISA tool"

154	
155	Root `KERNELS.md` (opened 2026-09-29, G-stages) is the live plan for taking the WMMA kernels from 42.0 toward 55.5 TFLOP/s. Facts a session needs before touching it: the suite's best GEMM ran at 2813 MHz / 137 W where the `peak` probe ran 2899 / 110, so utilisation is quoted per clock (478 FLOP/clk/CU is the measured peak); the shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8` is 240 VGPRs, no spill, `BK_TILES 1`, no prefetch; both head-128 attentions spill 112–126 VGPRs. `cmd/probe` (RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats/asm) was deleted by accident on 2026-09-22 and restored 2026-09-29.
156	
157	G0/G1 (2026-09-29, research §0.6, §6.5): **no real kernel runs at 2899 MHz.** A video forward runs at 2600–2650 MHz and ~149 W (package-limited ~150 W), so its ceiling is 49.9 TFLOP/s, not 55.5; a 20 ms bench burst sees 2813. **32 busy CPU threads halve the GPU clock** and make a forward 1.67x slower: never run a CPU-heavy job (staging, audio decode, a test sweep) beside a device timing, and sample `hwmon/freq1_input` + `power1_average` around any in-pipeline number. The shipped GEMM's rate is flat from 1 to 3+ workgroups a CU, and ACO does not prefetch across K tiles.
158	
159	G2 (2026-09-29, research §2.9): the GEMM ships as `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`) for H3: K slabs staged through LDS at wave32, 4x4 tiles, eight waves, bit-identical, 74 → 80% per clock, a 480p forward 29.9 → 27.1 s. G8 (same day) carried it to all nine hosts through their own gates: image step 2179 → 2058 ms, VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev fp16 at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; it loses below ~1000 rows ([[lds-gemm-needs-a-full-machine]]). The mechanism and what it rules out: [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]]; the screen: [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].
160	
161	G5 (2026-09-29, research §2.11): started as "Q4 B fragments built in registers" and measured out of it before it was built. On the LLM's MoE up GEMM (`llm_moe_gemm.comp`) the LDS round trip is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings already runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read 2–8x. The K loop as a software pipeline with each block's bytes fetched once (`-DPIPE=2`) is bit-identical, `moe.up` 1.68x at 2048 tokens, whole-model prefill 1194 → 1407 tok/s. The same pipeline on the down mode moves Q5_1 by nothing and IQ4_NL by 1.05x (shipped for IQ4_NL only). Lesson: price a kernel's parts by their absence (`MOE_*` knobs, `LLM_MOE_SPV`, [[moe-gemm-screening]]) before building the arm the plan names; a two-set (ping-pong) register pipeline spilled and lost, the one-set form won.
162	
163	G5c (2026-09-30, research §2.12): the padding. The permutation aligns experts to one fragment (16 rows) instead of the widest row block, and every single-wave build of `llm_moe_gemm.comp` is a `SHORT` build that runs one of WM copies of its K loop from the record's real-row count, bit-identical: the padding factor at 2048 tokens 1.90x → 1.19x, `moe.down` 1.23x (1.28x on IQ4_NL), `moe.up` 1.11x, prefill 1417 → 1514 tok/s at 2048; the m2/m4 boundary moved to 256 tokens. Two facts: any third copy of the Q4_K up m4 loop spills 15 registers and costs 9% on full blocks (it ships 2- and 4-tile copies, the store bounded by the real count), and a short tile's rows are cheap rows (0.086 vs 0.137 µs) because the slab unpack, ~300 VALU a lane a step, is now the largest term in the up projection. Next on that kernel: the unpack's VALU.
164	
165	**Why:** eight verticals ended on "the GEMMs are at their ceiling" without the ceiling ever being pushed; a GEMM win lands in every served request.
166	
167	**How to apply:** file a closed finding under the next free `§N.M` in `research/` and point the G-stage at it; prove a lever in `gemm_wmma.comp`'s suite first, ship it in `dit_gemm.comp`, and screen it with each vertical's own tool ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]]).
168	
169	**2026-09-30 (G4, §3.8):** the transposed attention priced and left as shipped — the honest floor is 81% per clock (87–90% with L0 hits), the softmax 6–7 points, the K/V loads 11–12, and five bit-identical arms all inside ±2% of the shipped build; G4b (K/V slabs through LDS at QT1) is the one lever left, ≤ 2% of a forward. The kernel is opt-in on the image DiT (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`, 1.7% a step) because the edit oracle's prefill bound sits near its sensitivity floor. See [[attention-kernel-plateau]]. Next in the order: G6 (streaming kernels) or G3 (the epilogue).
170	
171	**G3 done 2026-09-30** (§2.14): the fp32 C store costs the matrix pipe nothing (`STORE_TILES` control, same per-clock rate); the M sawtooth is ≤ 5% past ~1300 rows; H3's `pack v` and `swiglu` passes are the LDS build's epilogue now (`C_PACK`, `C_SWIGLU` with `projGateUp` interleaved in 64-row groups; `zero_f16.comp` for the A pad rows), bit-identical, a 480p forward 26.2 → 25.6 s. The served binary restages its int8 cache once on redeploy. The SwiGLU fusion is carried to `qimage/dit` too (same session, 1.04–1.06x a cached step; the v store is not, a 19-row prefix puts fresh rows mid-tile). **Carried further the same day (G8, session 11):** `ace/dit` (a forward 1.07–1.10x; the fused gate|up runs the LDS build at *every* row count — its grid is twice a projection's — while the other projections keep the wave64 build to 1024 rows) and `h3/vae` (**a 480p decode 34.4 → 30.0 s, 1.15x**, the biggest carry of G3). Both bit-identical to the old binaries by output hash (`ACE_DIT_REF` on `TestGPUBits`; the `bits` log lines in `h3/vae`). Trap found on the VAE: where a host's bias rides in the GEMM (a ones column in A), a pad row of v's GEMM is the bias, not +0, and zeroing A's pad rows would take the ones column with it — so `C_PACK` runs only on batches of whole 128-row tiles there. Parakeet/kokoro priced and left (SiLU passes + v pack = 2.3% of a 13.5 ms encoder). Served binary still needs a redeploy. Next: G6 or G4b.

173	name: spec-loop-run
174	description: How to run the speculative decode loop in strix-halo-vulkan (`cmd/llm -spec`), what it costs, and the two things to read before believing its numbers.
175	metadata:
176	  type: project
177	---
178	
179	`go run ./cmd/llm -spec` (added 2026-09-19, P5c) stages the 48-layer trunk
180	**and** the 1.92 GB draft head and then runs two arms interleaved in one
181	process — a plain greedy loop and the speculative one — because P1c's
182	environment finding means a decode rate from a different day is not a control.
183	**~85 GB, ~31 s to stage the trunk plus ~1 s for the draft, then ~5 s per
184	128-token arm**; `-spec-passes 2` (the default) is four arms, so budget ~1200 s
185	and pass the shard path, not the directory (see [[llm-resident-run]]).
186	
187	- `-ctx 512` is the short arm; `-spec-prefix N` prompts with the first N tokens
188	  of `-ppl-file` instead of `-prompt`, which is the long arm. **Never above
189	  `-ctx 2048`** — the draft head refuses, for the reason in
190	  [[mtp-draft-head-run]].
191	- `-layers 4` is the 9 GB plumbing check: the mechanics work and the
192	  acceptance rate is 0%, because the draft head was trained against 48 layers.
193	- `SPEC_PLAIN_ONLY=1` drops the speculative arm and runs the plain loop
194	  against itself. It is the control on the control and it is not optional.
195	
196	**Two things to read before quoting a multiplier.**
197	
198	1. **The pairwise id table, including the plain-against-plain rows.** At the
199	   short context the plain loop **does not reproduce itself**: three plain
200	   runs over one prompt give three different texts, diverging at tokens 24 and
201	   98 — *deterministically*, the same three every invocation, so something
202	   survives `Reset` rather than decode being racy. It only shows where the
203	   previous run left cells past the next prompt's end. So "token for token" is
204	   only a claim about speculation when the plain rows are in the table too.
205	2. **The per-dispatch attribution the tool prints.** The multiplier is a
206	   ratio of two loops and the interesting number is which dispatch moved: it
207	   is what found that `moe.up` read 101 GB/s at two rows against 141 at one.
208	
209	**Why:** the stage's whole deliverable is a multiplier, and both of the ways
210	to get one wrong here are invisible in the headline — a control that is not
211	reproducible, and a regression hiding inside a block that everything else
212	disguises.
213	
214	**Set the shipped banks or the numbers are the wrong ones.** `cmd/llm` stages
215	the checkpoint's own widths unless `LLM_DENSE_BANK`/`LLM_MOE_BANK` are set the
216	way `cmd/serve` sets them (`LLM_BANK_CACHE` too, or P4c's re-fit is ~8 min).
217	Plain decode is 27.4 tok/s without them and 36.3 with, and the speculative
218	multiplier is **0.95x short / 0.89x long** on the shipped banks against
219	0.98x/0.98x without — narrowing the trunk makes speculation worse, because the
220	draft head stages at the checkpoint's own widths and does not shrink with it.
221	
222	**The loop is parked and costs the product path nothing.** The rollback's
223	120.75 MB of ping-pong slots is `GraphOpts.Speculative`, which only `-spec`
224	sets; `Speculate(true)` refuses on a graph without it. `-gen` measures 36.0
225	tok/s on 795.6 MB of arenas either way.
226	
227	**How to apply:** two runs of each context, `-csv results/p5c_spec_*.csv`, in
228	the foreground with nothing else on the GPU ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]]). The
229	answer as of 2026-09-19 is **0.95x**, so do not expect a run that says
230	otherwise without a code change behind it.

232	name: mtp-draft-head-run
233	description: How to run the MTP draft-head observer in strix-halo-vulkan (`cmd/llm -mtp`), what it costs, and the two traps that make its numbers wrong.
234	metadata:
235	  type: project
236	---
237	
238	`go run ./cmd/llm -mtp` (added 2026-09-19, P5a) stages the 48-layer trunk
239	**and** the 1.92 GB draft head (`blk.48` of
240	`models/.../mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4_K_M.gguf`) together: **~80 GB, 1m3s to
241	stage the trunk plus ~1s for the draft**, then ~28 ms a trunk step and ~7 ms
242	a draft step. It fits beside the running `ai` user service with ~2 GB spare —
243	`free -g` showed 106 used / 10 available mid-run — so nothing else large can
244	start beside it. Set `LLM_DENSE_BANK`/`LLM_MOE_BANK`/`LLM_BANK_CACHE` the way
245	`cmd/serve` does, or the trunk stages at L8a's 81.89 GB and will not fit.
246	
247	**Two traps, both found by measuring.**
248	
249	1. **`-mtp-free` degenerates.** Greedy decoding at temperature zero loops a
250	   paragraph verbatim within a few dozen tokens, and a looping trunk is
251	   trivially predictable: the free-running arm reads **92.2%** acceptance
252	   against the teacher-forced **74.0%**. Priming (`-mtp-prime`) does not
253	   prevent it. The tool prints the generated text for exactly this check —
254	   read it before quoting any free-running number.
255	2. **Never stage above n_ctx 2051.** `attention.compress_ratios[48]` is 0 in
256	   the draft shard, so the MTP layer's QSA budget is unknown; `NewMTPHead`
257	   borrows the trunk's 4 and refuses above the width where the selection
258	   stops being the identity.
259	
260	The instrument is **exactly deterministic** — two runs of the five-arm wiring
261	screen agreed count-for-count in all thirty cells — so a single run is enough
262	and any difference between arms is real.
263	
264	**Why:** the acceptance rate is the number P5 turns on, and both traps
265	inflate it by 18+ points in the direction that would make the stage look
266	worth more than it is.
267	
268	**How to apply:** quote the teacher-forced arm
269	(`-mtp-n 1024 -mtp-depth 6 -ctx 2048`, ~3 min including staging), always with
270	the `zero` negative control beside it (~10%), and see
271	[[llm-resident-run]] for the residency rules and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] for
272	running it detached with nothing else on the GPU.

274	name: batched-rows-overlap
275	description: Batched decode runs per-row attention/DeltaNet dispatches side by side (vk.MultiDispatch.Overlap); per-label timings of an overlapped group land on its first dispatch; LLM_BATCH_OVERLAP=0 is the control.
276	metadata:
277	  type: project
278	---
279	
280	Since 2026-09-23 a batched pass (`Graph.DecodeRows`, C5) emits its rows'
281	per-sequence work stage by stage with no barrier between rows of a stage
282	(`vk.MultiDispatch.Overlap`). Attention gives each row its own 64-row
283	scratch slice (`AttnGPU.rowScratchFor`); the combine stays serialized
284	because it writes pad rows into the next row's context. 3 rows 48.4 → 46.2 ms.
285	
286	**Why it matters when profiling:** an overlapped group's GPU time is written
287	on its **first** dispatch, and the rest read ~0, so per-label ms (e.g.
288	`attn.attn.split` 33.7 us "each" at 3 rows) are not per-dispatch costs any
289	more. Compare blocks or whole passes, or rerun with `LLM_BATCH_OVERLAP=0`.
290	
291	**How to apply:** any new per-row dispatch in a batched pass must either
292	touch only row-private memory or be kept out of the overlap; the sparse
293	case of `TestGraphDecodeRowsIsEachSlot` is the race detector (shared scratch
294	failed it 3/3). See [[batched-rows-need-distinct-conversations]].

296	name: batched-rows-need-distinct-conversations
297	description: "Pricing a multi-row decode pass on one sequence's tokens (or a fixed token per row) understates the MoE; three real conversations touch 26.8 experts a layer and cost 64 ms, not 52."
298	metadata:
299	  node_type: memory
300	  type: feedback
301	  originSessionId: d0d0daa2-ca18-4cc0-a764-84e089efc230
302	  modified: 2026-09-23T11:35:30.496Z
303	---
304	
305	**2026-09-23, CONCURRENCY.md C5.** C5a priced a three-row pass with
306	`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 1,2,3`: **52 ms, 1.78 steps**. Those three rows are
307	three *consecutive tokens of one sequence*, which share experts. The server's
308	three concurrent agents ran **64 ms a pass**. `cmd/llm -batch` (one slot a
309	row, each prefilled with different wikitext) reproduced the 64 ms only once
310	it decoded greedily. Feeding each row a fixed token also read ~54 ms, because
311	a row that repeats its token reads the same experts every step. Three real
312	conversations touch **26.8 distinct experts a layer** against 10 for one row,
313	and the MoE is the part of a pass that grows with rows.
314	
315	**Why:** a batched pass costs the *union* of its rows' experts, and anything
316	that correlates the rows' tokens shrinks the union.
317	
318	**How to apply:** price batched decode with `cmd/llm -batch 1,2,3
319	-batch-depth 7000` (greedy, different text per slot), and check
320	`PassExperts` on the printed "distinct experts" line (~10/19/27 at 1/2/3
321	rows). The same trap applies to any rows-vs-cost claim about the MoE,
322	including P5's speculative verification rows, which *are* one sequence and
323	so priced correctly there. See [[concurrency-loadgen-run]] and
324	[[two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate]].

326	name: attention-kernel-plateau
327	description: The transposed WMMA attention (h3_attn_t.comp) is at a measured plateau — no exact arm beats the shipped build; how it decomposes (softmax 7, K/V loads 12, floor 81%), why the allocator's moves decide, and the image DiT's edit gate that sits near its sensitivity floor.
328	metadata:
329	  type: project
330	---
331	
332	KERNELS.md G4 / research §3.8 (2026-09-30): `h3_attn_t_qt2_kt4` runs at 73% per clock (37.3–37.8 TFLOP/s at 480p, 2650–2690 MHz). Gutting it honestly (results kept live, `GUT_*` knobs) puts the MMA+loads floor at 81%, 87–90% with every K/V load an L0 hit (`L0_LOADS`); the softmax is 6–7 points (the row max's 16-deep chain 7, the rescale 3), the K/V loads 11–12. Five bit-identical arms (`TAIL_SPLIT`, `QLDS`, `MAX_TREE`, `LAZY`, `PV_ORDER`) all land within ±2% of the shipped build at 480p and 768p — the best executes 135 fewer VALU and no spill reloads a block for the same time. Head split (1.5x MMAs) and wave64 (VALU two passes) are dead by arithmetic. The one lever left is G4b: K/V slabs staged through LDS for a workgroup's waves at QT1 (§2.9's lever), ≤ 2% of a video forward.
333	
334	**Why:** at 256 VGPRs the register allocator's ~200–390 moves a block redraw with every source edit and cost what the edit saves; the instruction count is an upper bound, not a price (as §2.13 found on the MoE GEMM). Screen arms against the shipped build's *time*, not its counts.
335	
336	**How to apply:** don't build more exact arms on this kernel without a structural register change; the screen is `TestGPUAttentionScreen` with `H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path` (it reports "bits: identical" against the shipped transposed build). On the image DiT the kernel is opt-in (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`): exact on identical inputs (rms 8e-5 a block), but `TestGPUEditOracle`'s prefill bound (2e-2) amplifies prefix-row fp16 differences ~100x at three target rows — a plain-family perturbation reads 1.73e-2, the transposed 7.9e-2. Before blaming a kernel on a gate like that, perturb the passing path with a same-family build and dump the context block by block (the kernel run at one block alone on the other kernel's inputs is the decisive test). See [[valu-costs-matrix-clocks]], [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

338	name: valu-costs-matrix-clocks
339	description: On this RDNA3.5 part every VALU instruction beside a WMMA costs the matrix pipe ~1 clock (~3% per instruction per MMA at wave32); the shipped LDS GEMM lost 7% to register-allocator moves; how to price a kernel's non-MMA work with the issue probe.
340	metadata:
341	  type: project
342	---
343	
344	Measured 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G-o8, research §2.10) with `shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp` run through `PEAK_SPV=... PEAK_MMAS=16 PEAK_SUBGROUPS=8 PEAK_WAVE=32 go run ./cmd/bench peak`: the WMMA runs on the SIMD's VALU, so 4 independent fp32 FMAs per MMA cost 12%, 8 cost 20%, linearly (a wave32 MMA is ~34 clocks). LDS fragment reads at the GEMM's ratio cost only 3%, a barrier alone 0, the two together 9% (the post-barrier burst). The shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` carried ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov` a tile (RA assembling the second K tile's fragments while hoisted staging loads held registers); keeping the K tiles as a `[[dont_unroll]]` loop (`KT_LOOP`) plus non-`readonly` staging views (`STAGE_RW`, with a never-taken store so `nir_opt_access` cannot re-infer readonly and sink the loads) removed them: 80 → 85% per clock, bit-identical.
345	
346	**Why:** every earlier GEMM lever counted bytes; nobody counted VALU issue, and it was the largest remaining term. `subgroupShuffleXor(v,16)` at wave32 is `v_permlanex16` (VALU, no LDS), so an exchange that halves LDS bytes still loses (−5%).
347	
348	**2026-09-30 (G5d, §2.13), two corrections to the rule.** The count is an
349	*upper bound*, not a price: cutting the MoE up GEMM's non-MMA VALU 331 → 259
350	a step (22%) bought 2%, because with four waves a SIMD one wave's VALU
351	overlaps another's MMAs part of the time, which the single-kernel probe never
352	saw. And read the ISA before estimating: ACO already fuses `float16_t(a*b-c)`
353	into one `v_fma_mixlo/hi_f16` (f16 sources through op_sel), so a dequant
354	element is 3 VALU, not 5 — and a nibble masked into a halfword is the f16
355	denormal `nib × 2^-24`, which `v_fma_mix` reads directly (RADV preserves fp16
356	denormals; scale by 2^24, exact). Allocator moves at the 256-VGPR limit are
357	not removable by the KT_LOOP trick everywhere: on that kernel it added them.
358	
359	**How to apply:** before timing any coopmat kernel build, `RADV_DEBUG=asm go run ./cmd/probe x.spv 32` and count `v_swap|v_mov|v_cndmask|v_perm` per `v_wmma`; the budget is a few per MMA. Prefer a loop the compiler cannot reschedule over an unrolled body. Dequant (G5) and attention (G4) arms are priced by the same rule. See [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

361	name: moe-gemm-screening
362	description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the three traps hit doing it (2026-09-29/30)."
363	metadata:
364	  node_type: memory
365	  type: project
366	  originSessionId: cd78a9a3-9df7-41bb-898c-6e666a202333
367	  modified: 2026-09-29T23:18:07.954Z
368	---
369	
370	`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
371	for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
372	embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
373	`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤256 tokens and
374	m4 above (moved from 1024 by §2.12), so a 2048-token screen must override
375	`up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build (WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one. The
376	shared expert runs the **Q8_0** builds of the same rungs (`up_q80_m4`,
377	`down_q80_m4`), so a screen that changes the schedule must load those too.
378	
379	**Why:** three traps cost time (KERNELS.md G5a/G5c, research/2.11, 2.12).
380	The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
381	from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. A `-moe` arm at
382	60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
383	samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean. And
384	since §2.12 the permutation aligns experts to **16 rows**, and every
385	single-wave build is a `SHORT` build that bounds its tiles by the record's
386	real rows: a build compiled **without** `-DSHORT=1` loaded through
387	`LLM_MOE_SPV` writes the next expert's rows unless `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` is set
388	(it is what the pre-§2.12 controls need). A SHORT build that rounds its tile
389	count up (`SHORT_STEP=2`) must still bound the *store* by the real count; the
390	first cut stored the rounded tiles and `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` caught it as
391	"every plan with m4 in the up position disagrees".
392	
393	**Two more (2026-09-30, G5d):** `cmd/llm -moe` needs `-model` as the *shard*
394	(`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`);
395	the directory default holds four GGUFs and every arm exits in a second with
396	"holds 4 checkpoints, name one" — four "done" lines in the same second is that
397	failure, not a fast run. And a passing gate through `LLM_MOE_SPV` proves
398	nothing until a wrong-by-construction build (`-DMOE_NIB_ONLY=1`) through the
399	same override has been seen to fail it. An arm at 60 iters over four token
400	counts is ~20 s wall including staging.
401	
402	**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
403	flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
404	against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
405	counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2)
406	and `TestMoEGPUPaddingIsInert`, then time; the whole-model identity is
407	`TestGraphLogits`'s diagnostics reproduced to the digit against an old test
408	binary built in a `git worktree` (symlink `models/` and `reference/out/`,
409	copy `shaders/*.spv`). A control that removes work can read above the pipe's
410	ceiling only if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the
411	disassembly before trusting it. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and
412	[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

419	
420	**The depth regression is closed, in four stages, all 2026-09-21.** Decode at
421	64 000 cells went **4.05 → 15.91 → 26.76 → 27.69 tok/s** and the falloff from
422	depth zero **0.14x → 0.48x → 0.76x → 0.79x**. Write-ups:
423	`research/p7-context-depth.md`, `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`
424	(which covers P8, P9 and P10). CSVs `results/p7_depth_*`,
425	`results/p10_depth_{base,p89,p8910}[_run2].csv`.
426	
427	48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 512 -tg 64`, ctx 66 880, `wiki.test.raw`,
428	three arms interleaved, two passes each (means):
429	
430	| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | pp |
431	|------:|----------:|-------:|-----------:|---:|
432	| 0 | 33.16 | 35.06 | **35.08** | 691 |
433	| 8 000 | 22.74 | 32.18 | **32.40** | 579 |
434	| 16 000 | 20.53 | 31.12 | **31.35** | 558 |
435	| 32 000 | 18.06 | 29.14 | **29.68** | 532 |
436	| 64 000 | 15.91 | 26.76 | **27.69** | 440 |
437	
438	A decode step at 64k: **62.9 → 36.1 ms**. The attention block across twelve
439	layers: **30.80 → 7.28 ms** a token (4.23x).
440	
441	**What each stage removed.**
442	
443	1. **P7 — `nKV` is the allocated cache, not the context.** Three kernels
444	   looped on it, paid in full *at depth zero*; and QSA was a mask and never a
445	   skip. See its own write-up — both are easy to reintroduce.
446	2. **P8/P9/P10 — at decode the kernels are single waves that all fit at
447	   once.** See [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]]; this is the reusable one.
448	   P8 splits the attention's key axis 16 ways (strided, constant count,
449	   folded by `llm_attn_combine.comp`); P9 splits the indexer's score from its
450	   cell expansion so both can stripe; P10 widens the *selection* from four
451	   waves to sixteen, because a radix select is a reduction and cannot be
452	   striped at all — the only parallelism left is waves on its one CU.
453	
454	**Prefill is untouched by P8/P9 and that is the control** — 692.6 → 690.5 at
455	depth 0 and 438.8 → 441.9 at 64 000, inside the noise. Prefill's 0.63x
456	falloff is the quadratic term any dense attention has; llama.cpp has it too.
457	
458	**The gates after touching any of this**:
459	
460	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P7
461	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSplitMatchesUnsplit               # P8
462	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer  # P9, exact
463	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSelectWidthDoesNotChangeTheAnswer # P10, exact
464	    go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph
465	
466	`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS=1`, `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=1` and `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_WG=256`
467	are the control arms.
468	**P8 is not bit-identical** and is covered by `PinSchedule` with the other
469	five reassociating decode kernels; P9 **is** bit-identical.
470	
471	**Superseded for prefill by P13 and then P14 (both 2026-09-22)** — 128k completes, and the
472	attention rung at depth is now `qt1_kt1`: see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
473	for the rates out to 128 000 cells — 128k prefills past 900 tok/s now and the
474	attention rung at depth is the **gathered** kernel, not a block one. The decode
475	table below stands, and decode is P14's control: it did not move.
476	
477	**Superseded for decode by P15 (2026-09-22)** — see
478	[[decode-at-depth-after-p15]] for the table that stands now: decode at 128k is
479	**27.20 tok/s** and the falloff **0.91x**, and the three things that got it
480	there were a *host* function, a stripe count and the gather+split composition.
481	The paragraph below is what P10 left and is kept for the P7-P10 attribution.
482	
483	**Still open as of P10**: **the gather** is now the only large item — of the 5.9 ms a
484	decode step still gains between depth 0 and 64k, the split attention is 3.0,
485	because the split shortened the walk sixteenfold without stopping it being a
486	walk over every key block. More slices is **not** the answer and that is
487	measured: 0.318 / 0.288 / 0.291 / 0.283 ms at 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 slices while
488	the combine climbs 0.004 / 0.006 / 0.010 / 0.018. **128 000 still does not
489	complete**
490	— the fill dies at ~115k in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth; the
491	untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional.
492	
493	**How to apply:** quote this table, not P7's and not the 2026-09-19 one; never
494	compare two depth-0 rates measured at different `-ctx`. Needs
495	`LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
496	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

---
name: decode-at-depth-after-p15
description: "Decode rates against context depth after P16 (2026-09-22): 34.4 tok/s at depth zero, 31.5 at 128k, the wide-batch cost that was a padding bug, the four depth terms and the control knobs."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dedbcc64-a855-44f2-a0fa-3d37d0946061
  modified: 2026-09-22T15:25:15.756Z
---

**P17 (2026-09-22) adds ~2% at depth** (128k 31.62 → 32.21, 64k 32.17 →
32.97, bit-identical: heads-on-rows at one row folds the same cells in the same
order, and the mask dispatch is deleted). **P17-3** takes decode's `attn.select` at
128k from 54.0 to 43.8 µs a layer: keys held in registers (`KREG`) plus a 10-bit
digit, exact, decode 32.93 → 33.16. Control `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=base`. What
is left of the select is ~13 µs of emit/setup. **The host n-gram gather at
decode is a tail**: median 236 µs, but 2 of 32 steps take ~8.7 ms at fixed token
positions, with ordinary fault counts and no GC, and those are 75% of the line. It
did not reproduce in isolation, and explaining it needs a kernel trace this
account can't take. `MADV_WILLNEED` is inert, and a pre-read table does not survive
staging, so the practical fix is residency, a deployment decision.

**Quote this table for decode — P16's (2026-09-22), not P15's.** 48 layers,
shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, two passes to
0.3%, write-up `research/p16-decode-arena-width.md`.

| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | P15 tg |
|------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|
| 0 | 1155.8 | **34.39** | 29.73 |
| 8 000 | 973.9 | 33.54 | 28.78 |
| 32 000 | 919.7 | 33.20 | 28.72 |
| 64 000 | 896.3 | 32.41 | 28.14 |
| 128 000 | 834.4 | **31.53** | 27.20 |

At ubatch 4096 (`-ctx 141000`, three depths — five overflow the descriptor):
0 → 1292.5 / 33.01, 64k → 979.4 / 33.00, **128k → 904.6 / 31.63**.

**P16's lesson, which generalises: a knob that costs decode is found by a
per-label diff between the two arms, not by theorising.** The wide-arena cost
was blamed on memory residency for two passes (P12-7, P15); `-depth -ubatch`
(arena rows separate from `-pp`) showed it followed the arena, and the label
diff put all of it on `move`, `dn.qkv`, `attn.qkv` in one look — the input
ports padded a one-row decode step with zeros to the whole arena. A padding
that is *correct* and slow is invisible to every tolerance test; it is gated
now by `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena`. Also P16: `hc.cn` runs a workgroup a
(token, stream) at ≤ 64 rows (`LLM_HC_CN_SPLIT_ROWS`, 0 = P11's grid), and
`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks (68 → 55 µs at 128k); its passes are neither
load-latency- nor atomic-contention-bound (both measured, 0.96x and 0.69x).

**The P15 section below still stands for what it explains** (the four depth
terms), with P16's rates on top.

**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:

- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
  depth-scaling term left on the device

**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**

**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:

    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step

**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
[[context-depth-rates]]):

    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch

**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.

**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.
---
name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
places).

The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.

So at decode:

- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
  concurrently.
- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
  nothing.)
- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.

Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.

**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.

**A prefill-shaped grid breaks this rule silently** (P16, 2026-09-22): P11
merged `hc.cn` to one workgroup a token for prefill bandwidth, which at decode
made it one workgroup walking four streams — 25 µs where a stream a workgroup
is 7. When a kernel is re-gridded for prefill, re-time it at `rows == 1`.

---
name: kernels-vertical-reopened
description: "The kernel-optimisation vertical was reopened 2026-09-29 as root KERNELS.md (G-stages); the ceiling is per clock, and cmd/probe is the ISA tool"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 18123f91-ab01-40e1-b663-e0bf82d8c3e6
  modified: 2026-09-30T14:00:00.000Z
---

Root `KERNELS.md` (opened 2026-09-29, G-stages) is the live plan for taking the WMMA kernels from 42.0 toward 55.5 TFLOP/s. Facts a session needs before touching it: the suite's best GEMM ran at 2813 MHz / 137 W where the `peak` probe ran 2899 / 110, so utilisation is quoted per clock (478 FLOP/clk/CU is the measured peak); the shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8` is 240 VGPRs, no spill, `BK_TILES 1`, no prefetch; both head-128 attentions spill 112–126 VGPRs. `cmd/probe` (RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats/asm) was deleted by accident on 2026-09-22 and restored 2026-09-29.

G0/G1 (2026-09-29, research §0.6, §6.5): **no real kernel runs at 2899 MHz.** A video forward runs at 2600–2650 MHz and ~149 W (package-limited ~150 W), so its ceiling is 49.9 TFLOP/s, not 55.5; a 20 ms bench burst sees 2813. **32 busy CPU threads halve the GPU clock** and make a forward 1.67x slower: never run a CPU-heavy job (staging, audio decode, a test sweep) beside a device timing, and sample `hwmon/freq1_input` + `power1_average` around any in-pipeline number. The shipped GEMM's rate is flat from 1 to 3+ workgroups a CU, and ACO does not prefetch across K tiles.

G2 (2026-09-29, research §2.9): the GEMM ships as `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`) for H3: K slabs staged through LDS at wave32, 4x4 tiles, eight waves, bit-identical, 74 → 80% per clock, a 480p forward 29.9 → 27.1 s. G8 (same day) carried it to all nine hosts through their own gates: image step 2179 → 2058 ms, VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev fp16 at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; it loses below ~1000 rows ([[lds-gemm-needs-a-full-machine]]). The mechanism and what it rules out: [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]]; the screen: [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

G5 (2026-09-29, research §2.11): started as "Q4 B fragments built in registers" and measured out of it before it was built. On the LLM's MoE up GEMM (`llm_moe_gemm.comp`) the LDS round trip is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings already runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read 2–8x. The K loop as a software pipeline with each block's bytes fetched once (`-DPIPE=2`) is bit-identical, `moe.up` 1.68x at 2048 tokens, whole-model prefill 1194 → 1407 tok/s. The same pipeline on the down mode moves Q5_1 by nothing and IQ4_NL by 1.05x (shipped for IQ4_NL only). Lesson: price a kernel's parts by their absence (`MOE_*` knobs, `LLM_MOE_SPV`, [[moe-gemm-screening]]) before building the arm the plan names; a two-set (ping-pong) register pipeline spilled and lost, the one-set form won.

G5c (2026-09-30, research §2.12): the padding. The permutation aligns experts to one fragment (16 rows) instead of the widest row block, and every single-wave build of `llm_moe_gemm.comp` is a `SHORT` build that runs one of WM copies of its K loop from the record's real-row count, bit-identical: the padding factor at 2048 tokens 1.90x → 1.19x, `moe.down` 1.23x (1.28x on IQ4_NL), `moe.up` 1.11x, prefill 1417 → 1514 tok/s at 2048; the m2/m4 boundary moved to 256 tokens. Two facts: any third copy of the Q4_K up m4 loop spills 15 registers and costs 9% on full blocks (it ships 2- and 4-tile copies, the store bounded by the real count), and a short tile's rows are cheap rows (0.086 vs 0.137 µs) because the slab unpack, ~300 VALU a lane a step, is now the largest term in the up projection. Next on that kernel: the unpack's VALU.

**Why:** eight verticals ended on "the GEMMs are at their ceiling" without the ceiling ever being pushed; a GEMM win lands in every served request.

**How to apply:** file a closed finding under the next free `§N.M` in `research/` and point the G-stage at it; prove a lever in `gemm_wmma.comp`'s suite first, ship it in `dit_gemm.comp`, and screen it with each vertical's own tool ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]]).

**2026-09-30 (G4, §3.8):** the transposed attention priced and left as shipped — the honest floor is 81% per clock (87–90% with L0 hits), the softmax 6–7 points, the K/V loads 11–12, and five bit-identical arms all inside ±2% of the shipped build; G4b (K/V slabs through LDS at QT1) is the one lever left, ≤ 2% of a forward. The kernel is opt-in on the image DiT (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`, 1.7% a step) because the edit oracle's prefill bound sits near its sensitivity floor. See [[attention-kernel-plateau]]. Next in the order: G6 (streaming kernels) or G3 (the epilogue).

**G3 done 2026-09-30** (§2.14): the fp32 C store costs the matrix pipe nothing (`STORE_TILES` control, same per-clock rate); the M sawtooth is ≤ 5% past ~1300 rows; H3's `pack v` and `swiglu` passes are the LDS build's epilogue now (`C_PACK`, `C_SWIGLU` with `projGateUp` interleaved in 64-row groups; `zero_f16.comp` for the A pad rows), bit-identical, a 480p forward 26.2 → 25.6 s. The served binary restages its int8 cache once on redeploy. The SwiGLU fusion is carried to `qimage/dit` too (same session, 1.04–1.06x a cached step; the v store is not, a 19-row prefix puts fresh rows mid-tile). **Carried further the same day (G8, session 11):** `ace/dit` (a forward 1.07–1.10x; the fused gate|up runs the LDS build at *every* row count — its grid is twice a projection's — while the other projections keep the wave64 build to 1024 rows) and `h3/vae` (**a 480p decode 34.4 → 30.0 s, 1.15x**, the biggest carry of G3). Both bit-identical to the old binaries by output hash (`ACE_DIT_REF` on `TestGPUBits`; the `bits` log lines in `h3/vae`). Trap found on the VAE: where a host's bias rides in the GEMM (a ones column in A), a pad row of v's GEMM is the bias, not +0, and zeroing A's pad rows would take the ones column with it — so `C_PACK` runs only on batches of whole 128-row tiles there. Parakeet/kokoro priced and left (SiLU passes + v pack = 2.3% of a 13.5 ms encoder). Served binary still needs a redeploy. Next: G6 or G4b.

name: spec-loop-run
description: How to run the speculative decode loop in strix-halo-vulkan (`cmd/llm -spec`), what it costs, and the two things to read before believing its numbers.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`go run ./cmd/llm -spec` (added 2026-09-19, P5c) stages the 48-layer trunk
**and** the 1.92 GB draft head and then runs two arms interleaved in one
process — a plain greedy loop and the speculative one — because P1c's
environment finding means a decode rate from a different day is not a control.
**~85 GB, ~31 s to stage the trunk plus ~1 s for the draft, then ~5 s per
128-token arm**; `-spec-passes 2` (the default) is four arms, so budget ~1200 s
and pass the shard path, not the directory (see [[llm-resident-run]]).

- `-ctx 512` is the short arm; `-spec-prefix N` prompts with the first N tokens
  of `-ppl-file` instead of `-prompt`, which is the long arm. **Never above
  `-ctx 2048`** — the draft head refuses, for the reason in
  [[mtp-draft-head-run]].
- `-layers 4` is the 9 GB plumbing check: the mechanics work and the
  acceptance rate is 0%, because the draft head was trained against 48 layers.
- `SPEC_PLAIN_ONLY=1` drops the speculative arm and runs the plain loop
  against itself. It is the control on the control and it is not optional.

**Two things to read before quoting a multiplier.**

1. **The pairwise id table, including the plain-against-plain rows.** At the
   short context the plain loop **does not reproduce itself**: three plain
   runs over one prompt give three different texts, diverging at tokens 24 and
   98 — *deterministically*, the same three every invocation, so something
   survives `Reset` rather than decode being racy. It only shows where the
   previous run left cells past the next prompt's end. So "token for token" is
   only a claim about speculation when the plain rows are in the table too.
2. **The per-dispatch attribution the tool prints.** The multiplier is a
   ratio of two loops and the interesting number is which dispatch moved: it
   is what found that `moe.up` read 101 GB/s at two rows against 141 at one.

**Why:** the stage's whole deliverable is a multiplier, and both of the ways
to get one wrong here are invisible in the headline — a control that is not
reproducible, and a regression hiding inside a block that everything else
disguises.

**Set the shipped banks or the numbers are the wrong ones.** `cmd/llm` stages
the checkpoint's own widths unless `LLM_DENSE_BANK`/`LLM_MOE_BANK` are set the
way `cmd/serve` sets them (`LLM_BANK_CACHE` too, or P4c's re-fit is ~8 min).
Plain decode is 27.4 tok/s without them and 36.3 with, and the speculative
multiplier is **0.95x short / 0.89x long** on the shipped banks against
0.98x/0.98x without — narrowing the trunk makes speculation worse, because the
draft head stages at the checkpoint's own widths and does not shrink with it.

**The loop is parked and costs the product path nothing.** The rollback's
120.75 MB of ping-pong slots is `GraphOpts.Speculative`, which only `-spec`
sets; `Speculate(true)` refuses on a graph without it. `-gen` measures 36.0
tok/s on 795.6 MB of arenas either way.

**How to apply:** two runs of each context, `-csv results/p5c_spec_*.csv`, in
the foreground with nothing else on the GPU ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]]). The
answer as of 2026-09-19 is **0.95x**, so do not expect a run that says
otherwise without a code change behind it.
---
name: mtp-draft-head-run
description: How to run the MTP draft-head observer in strix-halo-vulkan (`cmd/llm -mtp`), what it costs, and the two traps that make its numbers wrong.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`go run ./cmd/llm -mtp` (added 2026-09-19, P5a) stages the 48-layer trunk
**and** the 1.92 GB draft head (`blk.48` of
`models/.../mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4_K_M.gguf`) together: **~80 GB, 1m3s to
stage the trunk plus ~1s for the draft**, then ~28 ms a trunk step and ~7 ms
a draft step. It fits beside the running `ai` user service with ~2 GB spare —
`free -g` showed 106 used / 10 available mid-run — so nothing else large can
start beside it. Set `LLM_DENSE_BANK`/`LLM_MOE_BANK`/`LLM_BANK_CACHE` the way
`cmd/serve` does, or the trunk stages at L8a's 81.89 GB and will not fit.

**Two traps, both found by measuring.**

1. **`-mtp-free` degenerates.** Greedy decoding at temperature zero loops a
   paragraph verbatim within a few dozen tokens, and a looping trunk is
   trivially predictable: the free-running arm reads **92.2%** acceptance
   against the teacher-forced **74.0%**. Priming (`-mtp-prime`) does not
   prevent it. The tool prints the generated text for exactly this check —
   read it before quoting any free-running number.
2. **Never stage above n_ctx 2051.** `attention.compress_ratios[48]` is 0 in
   the draft shard, so the MTP layer's QSA budget is unknown; `NewMTPHead`
   borrows the trunk's 4 and refuses above the width where the selection
   stops being the identity.

The instrument is **exactly deterministic** — two runs of the five-arm wiring
screen agreed count-for-count in all thirty cells — so a single run is enough
and any difference between arms is real.

**Why:** the acceptance rate is the number P5 turns on, and both traps
inflate it by 18+ points in the direction that would make the stage look
worth more than it is.

**How to apply:** quote the teacher-forced arm
(`-mtp-n 1024 -mtp-depth 6 -ctx 2048`, ~3 min including staging), always with
the `zero` negative control beside it (~10%), and see
[[llm-resident-run]] for the residency rules and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] for
running it detached with nothing else on the GPU.
---
name: batched-rows-overlap
description: Batched decode runs per-row attention/DeltaNet dispatches side by side (vk.MultiDispatch.Overlap); per-label timings of an overlapped group land on its first dispatch; LLM_BATCH_OVERLAP=0 is the control.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Since 2026-09-23 a batched pass (`Graph.DecodeRows`, C5) emits its rows'
per-sequence work stage by stage with no barrier between rows of a stage
(`vk.MultiDispatch.Overlap`). Attention gives each row its own 64-row
scratch slice (`AttnGPU.rowScratchFor`); the combine stays serialized
because it writes pad rows into the next row's context. 3 rows 48.4 → 46.2 ms.

**Why it matters when profiling:** an overlapped group's GPU time is written
on its **first** dispatch, and the rest read ~0, so per-label ms (e.g.
`attn.attn.split` 33.7 us "each" at 3 rows) are not per-dispatch costs any
more. Compare blocks or whole passes, or rerun with `LLM_BATCH_OVERLAP=0`.

**How to apply:** any new per-row dispatch in a batched pass must either
touch only row-private memory or be kept out of the overlap; the sparse
case of `TestGraphDecodeRowsIsEachSlot` is the race detector (shared scratch
failed it 3/3). See [[batched-rows-need-distinct-conversations]].

name: batched-rows-need-distinct-conversations
description: "Pricing a multi-row decode pass on one sequence's tokens (or a fixed token per row) understates the MoE; three real conversations touch 26.8 experts a layer and cost 64 ms, not 52."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d0d0daa2-ca18-4cc0-a764-84e089efc230
  modified: 2026-09-23T11:35:30.496Z
---

**2026-09-23, CONCURRENCY.md C5.** C5a priced a three-row pass with
`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 1,2,3`: **52 ms, 1.78 steps**. Those three rows are
three *consecutive tokens of one sequence*, which share experts. The server's
three concurrent agents ran **64 ms a pass**. `cmd/llm -batch` (one slot a
row, each prefilled with different wikitext) reproduced the 64 ms only once
it decoded greedily. Feeding each row a fixed token also read ~54 ms, because
a row that repeats its token reads the same experts every step. Three real
conversations touch **26.8 distinct experts a layer** against 10 for one row,
and the MoE is the part of a pass that grows with rows.

**Why:** a batched pass costs the *union* of its rows' experts, and anything
that correlates the rows' tokens shrinks the union.

**How to apply:** price batched decode with `cmd/llm -batch 1,2,3
-batch-depth 7000` (greedy, different text per slot), and check
`PassExperts` on the printed "distinct experts" line (~10/19/27 at 1/2/3
rows). The same trap applies to any rows-vs-cost claim about the MoE,
including P5's speculative verification rows, which *are* one sequence and
so priced correctly there. See [[concurrency-loadgen-run]] and
[[two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate]].

name: attention-kernel-plateau
description: The transposed WMMA attention (h3_attn_t.comp) is at a measured plateau — no exact arm beats the shipped build; how it decomposes (softmax 7, K/V loads 12, floor 81%), why the allocator's moves decide, and the image DiT's edit gate that sits near its sensitivity floor.
metadata:
  type: project
---

KERNELS.md G4 / research §3.8 (2026-09-30): `h3_attn_t_qt2_kt4` runs at 73% per clock (37.3–37.8 TFLOP/s at 480p, 2650–2690 MHz). Gutting it honestly (results kept live, `GUT_*` knobs) puts the MMA+loads floor at 81%, 87–90% with every K/V load an L0 hit (`L0_LOADS`); the softmax is 6–7 points (the row max's 16-deep chain 7, the rescale 3), the K/V loads 11–12. Five bit-identical arms (`TAIL_SPLIT`, `QLDS`, `MAX_TREE`, `LAZY`, `PV_ORDER`) all land within ±2% of the shipped build at 480p and 768p — the best executes 135 fewer VALU and no spill reloads a block for the same time. Head split (1.5x MMAs) and wave64 (VALU two passes) are dead by arithmetic. The one lever left is G4b: K/V slabs staged through LDS for a workgroup's waves at QT1 (§2.9's lever), ≤ 2% of a video forward.

**Why:** at 256 VGPRs the register allocator's ~200–390 moves a block redraw with every source edit and cost what the edit saves; the instruction count is an upper bound, not a price (as §2.13 found on the MoE GEMM). Screen arms against the shipped build's *time*, not its counts.

**How to apply:** don't build more exact arms on this kernel without a structural register change; the screen is `TestGPUAttentionScreen` with `H3_ATTN_ONLY_SPV=1 H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path` (it reports "bits: identical" against the shipped transposed build). On the image DiT the kernel is opt-in (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`): exact on identical inputs (rms 8e-5 a block), but `TestGPUEditOracle`'s prefill bound (2e-2) amplifies prefix-row fp16 differences ~100x at three target rows — a plain-family perturbation reads 1.73e-2, the transposed 7.9e-2. Before blaming a kernel on a gate like that, perturb the passing path with a same-family build and dump the context block by block (the kernel run at one block alone on the other kernel's inputs is the decisive test). See [[valu-costs-matrix-clocks]], [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].
---
name: valu-costs-matrix-clocks
description: On this RDNA3.5 part every VALU instruction beside a WMMA costs the matrix pipe ~1 clock (~3% per instruction per MMA at wave32); the shipped LDS GEMM lost 7% to register-allocator moves; how to price a kernel's non-MMA work with the issue probe.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Measured 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G-o8, research §2.10) with `shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp` run through `PEAK_SPV=... PEAK_MMAS=16 PEAK_SUBGROUPS=8 PEAK_WAVE=32 go run ./cmd/bench peak`: the WMMA runs on the SIMD's VALU, so 4 independent fp32 FMAs per MMA cost 12%, 8 cost 20%, linearly (a wave32 MMA is ~34 clocks). LDS fragment reads at the GEMM's ratio cost only 3%, a barrier alone 0, the two together 9% (the post-barrier burst). The shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` carried ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov` a tile (RA assembling the second K tile's fragments while hoisted staging loads held registers); keeping the K tiles as a `[[dont_unroll]]` loop (`KT_LOOP`) plus non-`readonly` staging views (`STAGE_RW`, with a never-taken store so `nir_opt_access` cannot re-infer readonly and sink the loads) removed them: 80 → 85% per clock, bit-identical.

**Why:** every earlier GEMM lever counted bytes; nobody counted VALU issue, and it was the largest remaining term. `subgroupShuffleXor(v,16)` at wave32 is `v_permlanex16` (VALU, no LDS), so an exchange that halves LDS bytes still loses (−5%).

**2026-09-30 (G5d, §2.13), two corrections to the rule.** The count is an
*upper bound*, not a price: cutting the MoE up GEMM's non-MMA VALU 331 → 259
a step (22%) bought 2%, because with four waves a SIMD one wave's VALU
overlaps another's MMAs part of the time, which the single-kernel probe never
saw. And read the ISA before estimating: ACO already fuses `float16_t(a*b-c)`
into one `v_fma_mixlo/hi_f16` (f16 sources through op_sel), so a dequant
element is 3 VALU, not 5 — and a nibble masked into a halfword is the f16
denormal `nib × 2^-24`, which `v_fma_mix` reads directly (RADV preserves fp16
denormals; scale by 2^24, exact). Allocator moves at the 256-VGPR limit are
not removable by the KT_LOOP trick everywhere: on that kernel it added them.

**How to apply:** before timing any coopmat kernel build, `RADV_DEBUG=asm go run ./cmd/probe x.spv 32` and count `v_swap|v_mov|v_cndmask|v_perm` per `v_wmma`; the budget is a few per MMA. Prefer a loop the compiler cannot reschedule over an unrolled body. Dequant (G5) and attention (G4) arms are priced by the same rule. See [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].
---
name: moe-gemm-screening
description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the three traps hit doing it (2026-09-29/30)."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: cd78a9a3-9df7-41bb-898c-6e666a202333
  modified: 2026-09-29T23:18:07.954Z
---

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤256 tokens and
m4 above (moved from 1024 by §2.12), so a 2048-token screen must override
`up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build (WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one. The
shared expert runs the **Q8_0** builds of the same rungs (`up_q80_m4`,
`down_q80_m4`), so a screen that changes the schedule must load those too.

**Why:** three traps cost time (KERNELS.md G5a/G5c, research/2.11, 2.12).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. A `-moe` arm at
60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean. And
since §2.12 the permutation aligns experts to **16 rows**, and every
single-wave build is a `SHORT` build that bounds its tiles by the record's
real rows: a build compiled **without** `-DSHORT=1` loaded through
`LLM_MOE_SPV` writes the next expert's rows unless `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` is set
(it is what the pre-§2.12 controls need). A SHORT build that rounds its tile
count up (`SHORT_STEP=2`) must still bound the *store* by the real count; the
first cut stored the rounded tiles and `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` caught it as
"every plan with m4 in the up position disagrees".

**Two more (2026-09-30, G5d):** `cmd/llm -moe` needs `-model` as the *shard*
(`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`);
the directory default holds four GGUFs and every arm exits in a second with
"holds 4 checkpoints, name one" — four "done" lines in the same second is that
failure, not a fast run. And a passing gate through `LLM_MOE_SPV` proves
nothing until a wrong-by-construction build (`-DMOE_NIB_ONLY=1`) through the
same override has been seen to fail it. An arm at 60 iters over four token
counts is ~20 s wall including staging.

**How to apply:** build arms with glslc to the scratchpad (the generate line's
flags from `shaders/shaders.go` plus the knob), `cmp` the knob-less build
against the shipped `.spv` (ids may differ; compare `cmd/probe` instruction
counts), gate with `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (maxAbs must be 0 against m2/m2)
and `TestMoEGPUPaddingIsInert`, then time; the whole-model identity is
`TestGraphLogits`'s diagnostics reproduced to the digit against an old test
binary built in a `git worktree` (symlink `models/` and `reference/out/`,
copy `shaders/*.spv`). A control that removes work can read above the pipe's
ceiling only if the compiler dropped MMAs; check the `v_wmma` count in the
disassembly before trusting it. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and
[[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

name: context-depth-rates
description: "Decode rates against context depth after P7/P8/P9/P10, what each removed, and the gates to run after touching attention; the gather is the last big item. Prefill and 128k are superseded by P13 (long-context-prefill-128k)."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**The depth regression is closed, in four stages, all 2026-09-21.** Decode at
64 000 cells went **4.05 → 15.91 → 26.76 → 27.69 tok/s** and the falloff from
depth zero **0.14x → 0.48x → 0.76x → 0.79x**. Write-ups:
`research/p7-context-depth.md`, `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`
(which covers P8, P9 and P10). CSVs `results/p7_depth_*`,
`results/p10_depth_{base,p89,p8910}[_run2].csv`.

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 512 -tg 64`, ctx 66 880, `wiki.test.raw`,
three arms interleaved, two passes each (means):

| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | pp |
|------:|----------:|-------:|-----------:|---:|
| 0 | 33.16 | 35.06 | **35.08** | 691 |
| 8 000 | 22.74 | 32.18 | **32.40** | 579 |
| 16 000 | 20.53 | 31.12 | **31.35** | 558 |
| 32 000 | 18.06 | 29.14 | **29.68** | 532 |
| 64 000 | 15.91 | 26.76 | **27.69** | 440 |

A decode step at 64k: **62.9 → 36.1 ms**. The attention block across twelve
layers: **30.80 → 7.28 ms** a token (4.23x).

**What each stage removed.**

1. **P7 — `nKV` is the allocated cache, not the context.** Three kernels
   looped on it, paid in full *at depth zero*; and QSA was a mask and never a
   skip. See its own write-up — both are easy to reintroduce.
2. **P8/P9/P10 — at decode the kernels are single waves that all fit at
   once.** See [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]]; this is the reusable one.
   P8 splits the attention's key axis 16 ways (strided, constant count,
   folded by `llm_attn_combine.comp`); P9 splits the indexer's score from its
   cell expansion so both can stripe; P10 widens the *selection* from four
   waves to sixteen, because a radix select is a reduction and cannot be
   striped at all — the only parallelism left is waves on its one CU.

**Prefill is untouched by P8/P9 and that is the control** — 692.6 → 690.5 at
depth 0 and 438.8 → 441.9 at 64 000, inside the noise. Prefill's 0.63x
falloff is the quadratic term any dense attention has; llama.cpp has it too.

**The gates after touching any of this**:

    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P7
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSplitMatchesUnsplit               # P8
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer  # P9, exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSelectWidthDoesNotChangeTheAnswer # P10, exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph

`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS=1`, `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=1` and `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_WG=256`
are the control arms.
**P8 is not bit-identical** and is covered by `PinSchedule` with the other
five reassociating decode kernels; P9 **is** bit-identical.

**Superseded for prefill by P13 and then P14 (both 2026-09-22)** — 128k completes, and the
attention rung at depth is now `qt1_kt1`: see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates out to 128 000 cells — 128k prefills past 900 tok/s now and the
attention rung at depth is the **gathered** kernel, not a block one. The decode
table below stands, and decode is P14's control: it did not move.

**Superseded for decode by P15 (2026-09-22)** — see
[[decode-at-depth-after-p15]] for the table that stands now: decode at 128k is
**27.20 tok/s** and the falloff **0.91x**, and the three things that got it
there were a *host* function, a stripe count and the gather+split composition.
The paragraph below is what P10 left and is kept for the P7-P10 attribution.

**Still open as of P10**: **the gather** is now the only large item — of the 5.9 ms a
decode step still gains between depth 0 and 64k, the split attention is 3.0,
because the split shortened the walk sixteenfold without stopping it being a
walk over every key block. More slices is **not** the answer and that is
measured: 0.318 / 0.288 / 0.291 / 0.283 ms at 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 slices while
the combine climbs 0.004 / 0.006 / 0.010 / 0.018. **128 000 still does not
complete**
— the fill dies at ~115k in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth; the
untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional.

**How to apply:** quote this table, not P7's and not the 2026-09-19 one; never
compare two depth-0 rates measured at different `-ctx`. Needs
`LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].
